transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. I guess I came in because... well, I just can't shake this thought. I've been an electrician for years, but if all that experience couldn't keep my own brother safe... it just makes me feel like I'm a real danger to anybody who works with me, or even the people living under my roof. I just don't know how to get past it.
Can you tell me how long ago the incident with your brother happened?
It was about four months ago. This has all just been going on since then... ever since the garage fire, and my nephew coming to live with us.
Since the fire, have you been having unwanted, vivid memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about that night?

Yeah, I have. It happens a lot. I'll just be in the middle of wiring a panel at work, or... or maybe I'll hear my nephew shut the garage door at the house. And suddenly, I'm right back there. I can actually smell the smoke. I see my brother. It's like... it's like the whole job site just drops out from under me, and I'm right back in that night.
Since the fire, have you been avoiding places, activities, or conversations that remind you of that night—like the garage, or talking about what happened?

Yeah, I have. I mean, I don't go in my own garage anymore unless I absolutely have to. I actually quit helping out with the electrical stuff at church, too. And... well, if people start talking about car projects, or they try to bring up the fire, I just shut them down fast. I just stay away from all of it.
Since the fire, have you noticed yourself feeling unusually jumpy, on edge, or easily startled—like you're always watching for danger, even in safe situations?

Not really, no. I mean... I'm not jumping at shadows or anything like that. I don't feel like I'm constantly looking over my shoulder for danger. It's more just... I just don't want to be around the things that remind me of it, like I said. But as far as being jumpy or easily startled, no, I haven't really noticed that.
Since the fire, have you noticed persistent negative feelings about yourself—like guilt or blame—or a loss of interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah, I have. It's... well, there's just this heavy mix of guilt and anger sitting in my chest pretty much all day. It doesn't really let up. It hits me the hardest when I look at my nephew. I just look at him and think about how he lost his dad in that fire, and now he's just... he got stuck with me instead. So yeah, the guilt is definitely there.
Since the fire, have you had trouble sleeping, noticed increased irritability or anger outbursts, or had difficulty concentrating?

Yeah, definitely the anger. Little things just set me off now. Like... if an apprentice at work asks me the same question twice, or if my nephew leaves his tools out. I just snap. I'll hear myself yelling and cussing at them before I can even pull it back. It just happens fast.
